newsitem.title: FRANCE: France decides against new legislation on cults.
newsitem.headline: France decides against new legislation on cults.

text.p: France required no further legislation to counter the dangers of religious cults, Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Wednesday when he formally launched a new watchdog body to monitor the activities of such groups.
"It is not our intention to set up a repressive system against cults. Our goal is to do what we can, when preventive actions have failed, to assure that the law is strictly applied," Juppe said.

He set up the interministerial watchdog group at the suggestion of a special parliamentary commission following the grisly deaths of 16 members of the Order of the Solar Temple in southeastern France last December.
The government has also urged prosecutors and state officials to keep an eye on cults in their areas and use all available legal weapons to prevent abuses.

The parliamentary commission had concluded in a report that cults such as the Solar Temple had the potential to grow rapidly in France and it urged the government to keep a closer watch on their activities.
The report estimated that France had about 173 cult groups plus 800 other, smaller affiliated entities, and that total membership numbered about 160,000.
Juppe said the 30 members of the watchdog body was to collect and analyse information on cult activities in France and keep the prime minister and the public informed of its findings.
It is also expected to prepare recommendations on how to improve the government's battle against cult abuses, he said.

Prosecutors described the Solar Temple deaths 11 months ago as a mixture of murder and suicide in a macabre ritual in which most of the victims, including three young children, were given drugs and had plastic bags pulled over their heads before being shot. Fifty-three members of the cult had died in similar circumstances in Switzerland and Canada in 1994.
